summary: Junín has no region-specific statute, enforcement finding, incident series or institutional practice in the sourced material. The department stands under the national framework of Peru, and the national assessment applies to a trans visitor here.
tangentialFactors:
The three sources assembled for this record (Infobae Perú of 20 February 2025, the IDEHPUCP legal analysis of 15 April 2025, and Agencia Presentes of 22 July 2024) carry national-layer content only: a congressional restroom bill, a constitutional-law critique of it, and nationwide hate-crime counts for 2020 to 2023. None of their findings is attributed to Junín or to any locality within it, so no comparison between this department and others can be drawn from them.

The national hate-violence figures the sources report (54 killings of TLGBI people and 170 recorded rights-violation cases across Peru for 2020 to 2023) are raw counts for the whole country, with no per-capita or departmental breakdown; they cannot be read as a rate for Junín.
localsOnly: No resident-facing finding specific to Junín appears in the sourced material: no departmental ordinance, local registry practice, regional health service, or local institution is documented. Residents of the department stand under Peru's national legal and administrative framework, which the parent record carries.
outOfScopeNotes:

Unresolved and not sourced: any Junín-specific incident of anti-trans violence, any departmental police or prosecutorial practice, and any local court ruling. The inventory contains no such data, and the absence of records here is not evidence of their non-existence.

Unresolved and not sourced: whether the hate-crime and homicide counts reported for Peru for 2020 to 2023 include any case arising in Junín; the sources give no geographic distribution.
